Extract Tag Key:Value Pairs into Individual Columns

Source: R/extract_tags.R
extract_tags.Rd

Parses pipe-delimited key:value tag columns (such as deploymentTags or observationTags) in a Camtrap DP-formatted dataframe and expands each unique key into its own column, appended to the right-hand side of the input dataframe.

Usage

extract_tags(df, col = NULL, keep_original = TRUE)

Arguments

df

A dataframe containing a tags column. Typically a Camtrap DP deployments or observations table.

col

Optional character string naming the tags column to parse. If NULL (the default), the function auto-detects by looking for a column named deploymentTags or observationTags. If neither or both are found and col is NULL, an informative error is thrown asking the user to specify col explicitly. A dataframe containing both columns is non-standard Camtrap DP; a warning is issued even when col is specified.

keep_original

Logical. Default TRUE. If TRUE, the original tags column is retained in the output. If FALSE, it is dropped.

Value

The input dataframe with new tag columns appended at the right-hand side. The original column order is preserved. Each unique key found across all tag strings becomes a new column. Rows with no tags (NA or empty string) receive NA in all new tag columns. Literal "NA" values within tag strings are converted to true NA. Each new column is auto-coerced to the most specific type possible (numeric → logical → date-time); if coercion would introduce new NA values beyond those already present, the column is retained as character and a warning() is emitted identifying the column name and the values that prevented coercion.

Details

Tag strings are expected to follow the pipe-delimited key:value format used by Camtrap DP, for example:

"temperature:13 | moonphase:New_Crescent"

Pairs are split first on " | " (space-pipe-space) and then on the first ":" to separate key from value. Only the first colon is used as the delimiter, so values may themselves contain colons (e.g. datetime strings).

Type coercion is attempted in order: numeric, then logical, then date-time (ISO 8601 formats). Coercion is only applied if it does not introduce new NA values beyond those already present in the column.

Author

Zachary Amir & Claude Opus 4.5

Examples

# deployments of the Woomargama wombat project shipped with WildObsR
dp <- example_datapackages("NSW_Woomargama_wombats_Linley_2021-22_WildObsID_0010")[[1]]
dep <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "deployments")

# deploymentTags holds "key: value" pairs, e.g. the lure used and predator management
head(dep$deploymentTags, 3)
#> [1] "lure: none | predatorManagement: Posion bait"
#> [2] "lure: none | predatorManagement: Posion bait"
#> [3] "lure: none | predatorManagement: Posion bait"

# expand each key into its own column
dep_expanded <- extract_tags(dep)
#> Warning: Column 'lure' could not be safely coerced from character; retaining as character. Values that prevented numeric coercion: none
#> Warning: Column 'predatorManagement' could not be safely coerced from character; retaining as character. Values that prevented numeric coercion: Posion bait
head(dep_expanded[, c("deploymentID", "lure", "predatorManagement")], 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   deploymentID                  lure  predatorManagement
#>   <chr>                         <chr> <chr>             
#> 1 10_WildObsID_0010_2021_a_Cam1 none  Posion bait       
#> 2 10_WildObsID_0010_2021_a_Cam2 none  Posion bait       
#> 3 10_WildObsID_0010_2021_b_Cam1 none  Posion bait       

# name the column explicitly, and drop the original tags
dep_expanded <- extract_tags(dep, col = "deploymentTags", keep_original = FALSE)
#> Warning: Column 'lure' could not be safely coerced from character; retaining as character. Values that prevented numeric coercion: none
#> Warning: Column 'predatorManagement' could not be safely coerced from character; retaining as character. Values that prevented numeric coercion: Posion bait
